scope: Independent review of published temporal screen-probe SH evidence in Docs/Unreal/assets/lumen-sponza/temporal/{screen-sh,motion-screen-sh} against raw DumpGPU captures, plus the reusable decoder and root UI manifest.

acceptance.label: active placements and nine RGB SH coefficients decoded with source identities
acceptance.evidence: Independent reader (temporal-sh-review/verify_raw.py, no decoder import) parsed raw DumpGPU records and read the R11G11B10 ambient plus RGBA16F directional binaries directly from Resources for baseline (light), lightstep-032 (light) and camera-064 (motion). It rebuilt all 11,074 active placements (3,706 + 3,686 + 3,682) and compared all 27 coefficients per placement: 298,998 values, 0 over 1e-6, maximum absolute difference 5.000e-7 (published coefficients are rounded to 6 decimals). Six named probes per state (floor/arcade uniform and adaptive) are enumerated in raw-spotcheck.json. Source identities were resolved by resource name, not by a reused id: SH pass/resource ids are 530/00040000020002f16b10+00040000020002f16dd0 (baseline), 97/0003000001fffe37bdb0+0003000001fffe37c070 (lightstep-032) and 553/000400000249ea452eb0+000400000249ea453170 (camera-064).

acceptance.label: projected real-scene lobes use fixed declared units and scales over time
acceptance.evidence: Each experiment declares radius 60.0 cm, rosette radius 55 px and one fixed response-luminance scale: 1.4454 for screen-sh and 1.5239 for motion-screen-sh. lobes.npz contains one lobe_max value per experiment and all 5x10 (light) / 3x10 (motion) probes use it; signed coefficient and signed-luminance minima are negative (screen-sh -0.03150945, motion -0.03988460), clamped arrays are exactly max(signed,0) and nonnegative, and the manifest declares the negative display clamp. Recovered negative fractions 0.02580247 / 0.03580247 and display-saturated fractions 0.00975309 / 0.00967078 match the summaries. The two experiments' scales differ but neither changes within its own time series; the UI captions declare the matching per-experiment scale.

acceptance.label: output and decoder reusable by the main temporal collector
acceptance.evidence: The published decoder ran from the parent source path with --state NAME=PATH on one light state and one motion state. --stage all exited PASS for both (recompute-light-all, recompute-motion-all), and the recomputed active records match the published records exactly: 3,706 light-baseline and 3,682 motion-camera-064 active probes, maximum 27-coefficient difference 0.0, identical counts, view exposure, frame indices and screen positions. The JSON/NPZ schema and CLI --state path are therefore usable by a collector. Caveat: --stage data writes byte-identical coefficient data but exits 2 because its finite_nonempty_outputs self-check requires publish/figures/lobes_<state>.png; a collector must use --stage all or ignore that exit status.

independent_raw.selected_probes: 18 probes total, 6 per state: floor uniform atlas [27,42], arcade uniform [7,16] and [60,16], plus adaptive first/middle/last; each compared on all 27 coefficients. All selected max |diff| <= 5e-7 and all projection errors 0.0 px against the published screen_xy.
independent_raw.allocator_rule: active_bound = min(captured NumAdaptiveScreenProbes, MaxNumAdaptiveProbes, atlas_view_capacity - NumUniformScreenProbes); active adaptive count equals that bound in all three states, and finite entries beyond the bound are counted as stale and excluded from the active coefficient set.
independent_raw.projection_rule: stored TranslatedWorldPosition projected with the captured TranslatedWorldToClip and ViewRectMin/ViewSizeAndInvSize, row-vector v @ reshape(4,4); checked against the uniform tile formula (ViewRectMin + atlas*16 + integer Hammersley jitter + 0.5) and the adaptive AdaptiveScreenProbeData packed xy.

hashes.screen-sh: 21 publish/report files plus the renamed decoder.py entry: all 22 SHA-256 and byte counts match. decoder.py is the renamed decode_temporal_sh.py (87,099 bytes, cb76422d4afe98be54d628c271d21873888ddd63c1f396a7bab2dfe3cbfc3d07).
hashes.motion-screen-sh: all 15 listed publish/report files match SHA-256 and byte counts; this manifest has no decoder hash entry.
hashes.screenshots: 8/8 published screenshot paths exist and match the SHA-256 recorded in summary.json.
hashes.metadata_mutation: No published metadata was written or rewritten; the check read the manifests and files only.

matching_flags.checked_guards: matched_kind, matched atlas/world/screen/SH, distance, normal dot, tile footprint, incompatibility threshold, same_atlas_coord, physical_sampling_position_identical, geometric_incompatible, sh_delta_rgb and sh_delta_l2 were recomputed; no atlas change is labelled physically identical and every incompatible case is flagged.

figures.observations: Lobes are anchored to the floor and side-arcade regions on the captured Sponza screenshots, remain readable across states, and show magenta x-ray outlines for occluded parts. The lobe images carry only the ten focus lobes plus green/magenta focus markers; the all-active dot grid appears only in the separate active_* image. Rosettes use one fixed ring radius and one scale per experiment.

stage_all.light-baseline: PASS; 3,706 active, recomputed SH max diff 0.0
stage_all.motion-camera-064: PASS; 3,682 active, recomputed SH max diff 0.0

stage_data.cause: collect_manifest requires publish/figures/lobes_<state>.png even when --stage data does not render figures.

ui_manifest.discrete_timing_statement: All light-buffer/camera-buffer states state that updates are discrete and playback spacing does not represent elapsed rendering time.

findings.finding: The documented --stage data reuse path writes correct, byte-identical coefficient data but returns exit code 2 because the finite_nonempty_outputs check requires figure PNGs that this stage never renders. A collector that checks the exit status will treat data-only extraction as a failure. --stage all on one state passes and reproduces the coefficients exactly.

The motion-screen-sh report's reuse example still names the light states (--states baseline,lightstep-...); the motion dump contains camera-001 and camera-064. The explicit --state NAME=PATH form works for both experiments.

The light manifest lists and hashes the renamed decoder.py entry; the motion manifest has no decoder entry, although both set generated_by to temporal-sh/decoder.py. All listed motion data/figure hashes are correct, and the current decoder exactly reproduces the motion camera-064 coefficients, so this is a provenance metadata gap rather than data drift.

The light and motion experiments use different fixed response scales (1.4454 and 1.5239). This is declared per experiment and is fixed within each time series, but colors/radii are not directly comparable between the two experiments.
